title: Microsoft 365 admin center: rules that automate agent lifecycle management
summary: Hold for corrections: deletion is described as irreversible even though Microsoft documents soft deletion with a 30-day recovery window. Manager reassignment is overstated beyond Agent Builder agents, and the claim that blocking is the only lifecycle API is false. The flagged Block/Unblock and Publish/Reject labels are documented.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The rule builder is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Agent management rules > Add rule.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Agents** > **Settings** > **Agent management rules**, and then select **Add rule**.

claims.claim: No API for creating or listing these Microsoft 365 admin center agent management rules is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 agent management rules Graph API create list rules automated lifecycle. Read agent-settings and Package Management API overview; results also describe separate Entra Agent ID lifecycle-policy APIs, not this rule builder.
claims.fix: Replace the categorical 'nothing in Graph creates or lists them' with 'As of November 2026, Microsoft documents no API for configuring these admin-center rules.' Distinguish the separate Entra Agent ID lifecycle-policy APIs.

claims.claim: An agent can be blocked or unblocked through Agents > All agents > agent > Block / Unblock.
claims.quote:
Select **Agents** > **All agents**.
In the **All agents** page, select an agent from the list of agents.
In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select **Block** or **Unblock**.
claims.fix: The pre-check warning is cosmetic: both action labels are documented. Narrow the row's governs label to 'Manual block or unblock for an agent'; this path does not describe uninstalling or pinning.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
claims.fix: Label this preview/beta and block-only, not an equivalent for unblock, uninstall and pin. State that production applications are unsupported; delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All is required and application permissions are unavailable.

claims.claim: Tenant agent access is managed at Copilot > Settings > Data access > Agents.
claims.quote: Select **Copilot** > **Settings** > **Data access** > **Agents** to manage your organization's agents.
claims.fix: Retain the cited guide's route but also report the different route in https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-settings#user-access: Agents > Settings > User access.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of the tenant-wide who-may-use-agents setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 tenant agent user access settings Graph PowerShell API publish reject requests API copilot package; Copilot agent tenant user access PowerShell. Read agent-settings, admin guide, Package Management overview and update reference; package access is per-package.

claims.claim: Publish requests can be approved or rejected at Agents > All agents > Requests > Publish / Reject.
claims.quote:
Select **Agents** > **All agents** > **Requests**.
Select the requested agent and view the agent's details.
Next to the name of the agent, select the action to **Publish** or **Reject** the agent.
claims.fix: Insert the omitted item selection: Agents > All agents > Requests > agent > Publish / Reject. The pre-check's missing labels are present as separate actions, not a literal slash-delimited label.

claims.claim: An API for approving or rejecting these agent publishing requests is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 tenant agent user access settings Graph PowerShell API publish reject requests API copilot package. Read admin guide, Package Management overview and update reference; APIs list requests and change package audiences, but do not document approving or rejecting submissions.

claims.claim: The lifecycle-rule control is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote:
Review impacted agents before running the rule
In the rule details pane, choose all agents or select a subset of agents from the list. Run the rule to apply the template.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Condition-based lifecycle rules are included without another licence for Copilot-licensed tenants.
claims.quote:
Included with Microsoft 365 Enterprise, Business, Education, and Front Line Worker plans
| Automate agent lifecycle actions using conditions-based rules | Microsoft 365 Admin Center | Yes | Yes | Yes |
claims.fix: Cite the service description and name its Microsoft 365 plans rather than implying Copilot is the only qualifying subscription. Distinguish included rules from premium policy templates and Graph access, which the same table does not include in those base plans.

claims.claim: The base lifecycle-rule capability has cost none because it is included in existing licences.
claims.quote:
Included with Microsoft 365 Enterprise, Business, Education, and Front Line Worker plans
| Automate agent lifecycle actions using conditions-based rules | Microsoft 365 Admin Center | Yes | Yes | Yes |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Agent 365 extends management coverage across additional agent types and platforms.
claims.quote: Agent 365 works with agents built on Microsoft platforms and with agents built or acquired from third-party sources; and integrates with Microsoft 365 administration, identity, security, and compliance capabilities.
claims.fix: Cite the service description. Avoid implying Agent 365 is required merely to inventory connected-platform agents: the same table includes external-platform registry synchronization in Microsoft 365 plans. Identify premium coverage separately.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Agent management rules automatically apply lifecycle policy on administrators' behalf.
claims.quote: Leverage rules-based agent management to automatically enforce lifecycle policies, such as flagging ownerless agents, or blocking risky agents.
claims.fix: Cite this overview but report the more specific agent-settings documentation too: administrators review affected agents and run bulk actions, and Apply template is explicitly one-time, not scheduled. Do not promise unattended execution for every supported rule.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The settings rule builder has a configurable condition called 'block risky agents'.
claims.quote: Searched: agent management rules risky signals inactive delete notification audit reassignment reversible owner leaves unused store; "agent management rules" "risky" "delete". Read agent-settings and agent-management overview; no such builder condition label is specified.
claims.fix: Remove the quoted condition label. Attribute risky-agent blocking to the roadmap and management overview; say the settings documentation instead lists 'Block ownerless agents without usage' and does not specify the risky-agent condition or its signals.

claims.claim: An automatic inactive-agent deletion rule is currently available on this settings page.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 agent management rules risky signals inactive delete notification audit reassignment reversible owner leaves unused store; "agent management rules" "risky" "delete". Read agent-settings and agent-actions; Entra identity lifecycle policies are a separate feature.
claims.fix: Attribute automatic inactive-agent deletion to roadmap 481518 only. State that the current settings page does not list a deletion rule; make deletion-threshold advice conditional on verifying tenant capability rather than importing Entra identity-policy behaviour.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The ownerless-agent rule can transfer ownership to the previous owner's manager.
claims.quote: Transfer ownership by using a bulk reassignment action to the manager of the previous owner based on Microsoft Entra ID hierarchy

claims.where: summary; Scope; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The manager-reassignment rule applies generally to ownerless agents across the platforms listed in Scope.
claims.quote:
Reassign ownerless agents created with Agent Builder to manager
This rule only supports agents created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder.
claims.fix: Qualify manager reassignment everywhere as supporting Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder agents only. Label the platform list as registry coverage, not coverage of every rule.

claims.claim: Agent management rules support installing Microsoft agents.
claims.quote: Install selected agents for all users through a single bulk action

claims.claim: Rules support blocking ownerless agents without usage.
claims.quote: Admins can create a custom rule to block multiple ownerless agents that have no usage.

claims.claim: Rules support applying a template.
claims.quote: Use the **Apply template** action in an agent management rule to apply security policies to existing agents.

claims.claim: Rules support rejecting stale publish requests.
claims.quote: Admins can create a custom rule to reject multiple agent publish requests that are older than a specified number of days.

claims.claim: Install, block, unblock, uninstall and pin actions are available on every agent in the registry.
claims.quote: You can only pin agents that are deployed to some or all users.
claims.fix: Replace 'available on every agent' with 'available for eligible agents, depending on platform and deployment state'. Pinning requires prior deployment; agent-actions also says Uninstall may not appear when the agent is not installed.

claims.claim: Administrators can manually install agents.
claims.quote: You can install agents across the whole organization or for specific users or groups by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Administrators can manually uninstall agents.
claims.quote: You can uninstall first-party or external agents across the whole organization or for specific users or groups

claims.claim: Administrators can pin deployed agents for users.
claims.quote: As an administrator, you can choose to pin a deployed agent to the **Agents** list within Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: All agents offers a Missing an owner inventory filter.
claims.quote:
Select **Agents** > **All agents**.
Below Agent inventory, select Missing an owner.

claims.where: What's changing: blocking Agent Builder and Copilot Studio agents
claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects Copilot and other host apps such as Teams and Outlook.
claims.quote: It also affects availability and functionality in other host products, such as Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams, or other Microsoft 365 applications.

claims.where: What's changing: blocking SharePoint and Foundry agents
claims.claim: Blocking SharePoint or Foundry agents affects only their availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Researcher and Analyst can be blocked tenant-wide.
claims.quote: To manage their availability, block the agent for the entire tenant by using the **Block** action in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Researcher and Analyst cannot be scoped to users through Edit users.
claims.quote: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the **Edit users** panel is disabled.

claims.claim: The same settings page carries security-template, publisher access, sharing, user access and tag controls.
claims.quote:
**Agent and plugin access** - Specify which categories of AI agents and plugins are permitted for use within the organization.
**Security templates** - Create preset policies, rules, and allow lists for new AI agents to ensure consistency and compliance.

claims.claim: Agents built by departed employees keep running without an accountable owner.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 agent management rules risky signals inactive delete notification audit reassignment reversible owner leaves unused store. Read agent-settings and agent-registry-overview; ownerless shared agents are documented, but continued runtime across platforms is not.
claims.fix: Replace with 'Shared agents can become ownerless when their creator is deleted from the organisation, creating an ownership-governance gap.' Do not assert continued execution across all agent types.

claims.where: Why it matters: unused agents in the store
claims.claim: Agents nobody uses still appear in the store.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 agent management rules risky signals inactive delete notification audit reassignment reversible owner leaves unused store. Read agent-settings, agent-actions and registry documentation; no general store-persistence rule based solely on inactivity is stated.
claims.fix: Replace the unsupported persistence assertion with advice: 'Review unused agents to reduce inventory and governance overhead.'

claims.where: Why it matters: unused agents in audit scope
claims.claim: Unused agents remain in audit scope.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 agent management rules risky signals inactive delete notification audit reassignment reversible owner leaves unused store. Read registry documentation and the Microsoft 365 Admin Center Agent Management audit-activities excerpt; inactivity-based audit scope is not stated.
claims.fix: Remove 'and in audit scope'. The documented administrative audit events do not establish this general audit-coverage claim.

claims.claim: Agent risk assessments use Microsoft security signals.
claims.quote: Risk signals are sourced from: Displays the Microsoft security platforms contributing risk signals for the agent, such as Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Defender.
claims.fix: Cite the registry documentation and identify this as the registry's risk assessment, not proof of the specific lifecycle-rule condition. Keep the question about that rule's exact criteria open.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Reassignment grants the new owner rights over the agent.
claims.quote: The new owner gets full edit and delete permissions, plus access to any files the previous owner uploaded.

claims.claim: Automated deletion is irreversible for the agent definition.
claims.quote:
When you delete an agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center, the agent is soft deleted.
During the 30-day retention period, you can restore the agent or permanently delete it.
claims.fix: Replace with 'Admin-center deletion is soft deletion with a 30-day recovery window; permanent deletion cannot be undone.' The settings page does not document a separate irreversible automatic-deletion rule.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Blocking an agent removes users' access to it.
claims.quote: **Block and unblock** | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Deleted agents are unavailable to users.
claims.quote: A soft-deleted agent is unavailable to its maker and end users

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Users receive no notice of blocking or deletion unless administrators add a communication step.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "audit" "notifications"; "agent management rules" "reversible" "notification". Read agent-settings and agent-actions; neither states notification behaviour for these rule executions. Separate Entra identity policies do document notifications.
claims.fix: Replace the assertion with 'Plan communications for affected users; notification behaviour for these lifecycle rules is not documented in the cited pages.' Retain notification options as an open question.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Manager reassignment depends on the Microsoft Entra hierarchy.
claims.quote: Transfer ownership by using a bulk reassignment action to the manager of the previous owner based on Microsoft Entra ID hierarchy

claims.claim: The admin-center inventory covers Agent Builder, Copilot Studio, SharePoint, Foundry and connected platforms.
claims.quote: Specific platforms supported include: Microsoft Copilot Studio, SharePoint, Agent Builder, AI Foundry, Agents Toolkit, other Microsoft agentic types (such as Researcher), and non-Microsoft agentic platforms (such as Manus or Genspark).
claims.fix: Cite this overview and distinguish registry visibility from each rule's narrower applicability, particularly Agent Builder-only manager reassignment.

claims.claim: Government-cloud rollout dates for this roadmap item are not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "GCC" rollout date. Read roadmap 481518, agent-settings and Agent 365 service description; no item-specific government rollout date was found. The service description nevertheless lists GCC availability for condition-based lifecycle rules.
claims.fix: Keep the item-specific absence of dates but add that the current Agent 365 service description lists condition-based lifecycle actions as available in GCC. Do not imply government clouds are excluded.

claims.where: Scope: roles; Governance controls: roles link
claims.claim: Agent management requires an administrator with agent management permissions.
claims.quote: The **AI Administrator** and **Global Administrator** roles have tenant-wide visibility and governance authority

claims.claim: Ownerless-agent manager reassignment is reversible.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 agent management rules risky signals inactive delete notification audit reassignment reversible owner leaves unused store; "agent management rules" "reversible" "notification". Read agent-settings and agent-actions; no undo of this rule is documented.
claims.fix: Remove '(reversible)'. Administrators can perform further ownership assignments for eligible shared agents, but that is not a documented undo operation restoring a departed original owner.

claims.claim: Agent-blocking events can be used in a change log.
claims.quote: | Blocked Agent | BlockedAgent | An admin blocked an agent. Users in the organization can't use the agent. |
claims.fix: Cite the audit-activities reference and distinguish administrative action events from unverified automatic-rule execution or rule-definition history.

claims.claim: Agent-deletion events can be used in a change log.
claims.quote: Soft-delete, restore, and permanent-delete events are recorded in the audit log with information about the system that initiated the action.

claims.claim: The audit log can supply a change record of these rule configurations.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent management rules" "audit" "notifications"; site:learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities "Agent" "BlockedAgent" "DeletedAgent". Read settings and audit-activities excerpts; no reconstructable rule-definition/configuration payload is established.
claims.fix: Remove the claim that audit logs supply rule configuration history. Recommend recording rule definitions and changes manually until Microsoft documents the applicable rule-configuration events and payloads; do not confuse action events with rule definitions.

claims.claim: Blocking is the only lifecycle action with an API.
claims.quote: Block, unblock, and reassign ownership of packages.
claims.fix: Replace with 'The Package Management API supports block, unblock and ownership reassignment, plus package audience/deployment updates; the mutation endpoints are preview.' Cite the overview and distinguish individual actions from a rule-configuration API.

claims.claim: The block endpoint requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.where: Governance controls: Copilot Studio data policies
claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents are additionally governed by Power Platform data policies.
claims.quote: Use Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies in Copilot Studio to block publishing agents through Copilot Studio supported channels.

claims.where: Governance controls: Copilot Studio sharing limits
claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents are generally bound by Power Platform sharing limits in their home environment.
claims.quote:
You configure the sharing limits for agents as a Managed Environments control in the Power Platform admin center.
Sharing limits only apply to agents that require authentication.
claims.fix: Qualify this as configured sharing limits for authenticated agents in Managed Environments. They govern new sharing operations and do not retroactively remove existing access. Cite this sharing-controls page.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The controls table includes every control the governance checklist directs administrators to use.
claims.quote:
Run the **Missing an owner** and **Availability: No users** filters to size the backlog before any rule runs.
The controls table has rows for rules, manual blocking, user access and publishing requests, but none for these inventory filters.
claims.fix: Add an inventory-review row at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents documenting Missing an owner and Availability > No users, sourced to the cited admin guide. If manual deletion or reassignment remains checklist advice, add its documented control or clearly tie it to a documented rule.
